title: #16: a stuck ticket's page says that its group and the groups after it wait for the decision
objective: The page the issuer writes when a ticket gets stuck in an open group that waits for it under D-097 names that group and the groups after it in the chain.
outline: ticket_issuer.py Issuer.stuck(): after its save and before pool.report, read a snapshot; when the ticket's group is open and the predicate the D-097 ticket added says the stuck ticket holds it, append the line ('%s waits for this decision; groups after it in the chain: %s' with core/chain.behind(snap, gid) joined by ', ', or 'none'). Pages written elsewhere (an escalated revise, page=False) are out of scope.
test_plan: Verifier: cases for acceptance 1 and 2 in a new class named with this ticket's case mark in tests_devloop/test_issuer.py, between class PageSetsOfIssuerAndWriters and class Timeout. Acceptance 1: a loop case; pop DEVLOOP_TICKET, DEVLOOP_GROUP and DEVLOOP_SLOT from self.env; self.add(...), self.plan(...), self.controller(), then read the inbox rows with kind 'decision' and ref '1'. Acceptance 2: a unit test of Issuer.stuck() on a pool fixture (tickets #1 stuck and #2 ready in group g1, g1 open with members ['1', '2'], no other group; a stand-in Issuer whose pool.report records its call), checking the reported page text. Before the change (measured for acceptance 1): the page text is only '#1 is stuck (decision): need the user' (red); acceptance 2 is red the same way. Implementer: acceptance 3 with a unit test of stuck() on a pool fixture (group g1 open, #2 merged, nothing depending on #1) and a loop case with harness ticket #1 alone, plan worker {'1': ['blocked']}, in tests_devloop/test_issuer.py between class Timeout and class Revise.
notes: D-097 (docs/DECISIONS.md, 2026-11-24, the user's ruling on issue #16): 1. a group with a stuck ticket goes on to its regression without waiting only when no ticket directly depends on the stuck ticket and the group's other tickets are all done (merged); the stuck ticket then leaves the group and has no group. 2. Otherwise (a ticket directly depends on it, or the group has unfinished tickets) the group waits for the decision on it: it is not closed and no member is moved out. 3. A ticket with no group is placed by the main session and the user (ready, which group, or cancel); the controller opens no new group for it and puts it at no chain end. D-097 notes that the wait shows on the page; a run with --forever writes no idle page, so the stuck page is where the main session sees it. A ticket alone in its group does not hold it: point 1 holds (no other member is unfinished), chain.stuck_holds returns False and the controller moves it out, so its page has no line. Depends on the D-097 ticket of this hand-in (its predicate; without it the group would not wait and the line would be false). Group new-g2.
acceptance: Harness tickets #1 and #2 (#2 depends on #1), plan worker {'1': ['blocked']}, a controller run without --forever: the unacked decision page whose ref is '1' has a line 'g1 waits for this decision; groups after it in the chain: g2'.

Issuer.stuck() on a pool fixture where #1 holds its group and no group comes after it: group g1 open with members #1 (stuck) and #2 (ready), nothing depending on #1, no other group: the page text reported for #1 has a line 'g1 waits for this decision; groups after it in the chain: none'.

When the stuck ticket does not hold its group at that moment (nothing depends on it and every other member is merged or cancelled; this includes a ticket that is its group's only member, e.g. harness ticket #1 alone with plan worker {'1': ['blocked']}), the page has no such line.
token_basis: One function in ticket_issuer.py (~10 lines) using the predicate and chain.behind; 2 short loop cases and one unit test. Simple tickets #121-#129 recorded 0.26M-1.3M.
vision: 等我處理的事積了多少: the page says which groups wait for the answer, so the user sees what an unanswered page holds up.
removes: none: it adds one line to a page that already exists; it removes no gate, and the 'why does the chain not move' diagnosis the main session did by reading groups.

The user asked for these (2026-11-24: 「修新issue」). Each ticket names its issue number(s) in its title so the main session can close the issues after landing. Tests go in the area's own test file in tests_devloop/ (or a new file for a new area), using loop_harness.py; never a catch-all file. Each case should run in seconds. Grouping: place these as you judge (core/chain.py); #14 and #15 may share a cause, #16 is about groups.

## Issue #15: a restarted controller starts a second issuer for a running ticket
T (A at b5564f9, macOS): after a controller restart done as #11's answer recommends (SIGTERM to `ticket_controller.py --forever` only, children left running), the old issuer of #320 (pid 84547, started by the previous controller, ppid 1 after the restart, running r3-worker through a wrapper `alternate.sh -> agy.sh`) was not adopted: the new controller started a second `ticket_issuer.py --id 320` (pid 66766), which ran an r2-worker in the same worktree `t320` on `t/320`. The r2 worker saw the other run and handed in `blocked`; #320 went stuck. The orphan then began merging main into t/320 (20:15:17 local). It ignored SIGTERM (agy.sh waits for agy) and had to be SIGKILLed.
What the main session read in the code (inference, not measured):
- The controller adopts a live issuer by the ticket's `run` stamp (ticket_controller.py finish_jobs, osx.stamp_dead). A second issuer can only start after the ticket is back to ready: `_release_orphan` (stamp judged dead) or the issuer's own `release()` on a signal (ticket_issuer.py _go, Interrupted), which sets ready and round-1. The new issuer running r2 while the old one ran r3 fits the second: the old issuer got a signal, released the ticket (r3 -> round 2), and then did not exit - its interrupted_costs/stop_agents path may block on a wrapper that ignores SIGTERM, or the process went on to the merge step.
- Find out which, by reproducing with the loop harness (a fake agent command that ignores SIGTERM; stop the controller as T did; also signal the issuer). Write the measured cause in the ticket.
Wanted:
- A ticket never has two issuers at once: the issuer holds a per-ticket lock (flock on a file under the worktrees root, like gitx's worktree lock) for its whole life; a second issuer for the same id refuses at once (exit 2, one line) and touches nothing.
- An issuer that has released its ticket (interrupted) does no further work on it: no merge, no push, no pool write other than the release; it stops its agents' process trees (kill_tree, escalating to SIGKILL after a short grace when a wrapper ignores SIGTERM) and exits.
- A restarted controller adopts a live issuer (stamp alive) and does not dispatch the ticket again while that issuer (or its lock) lives.

## Issue #14: a ticket's worktree disappears during a chain fall-through after quota
T: three cases on 2026-11-24 (#369 reviewer, #351 worker, #354 reviewer): the first command of the role's chain (agy.sh) said "usage limit reached"; about 3 minutes later the next command (claude) could not start: `no command for reviewer could start (cannot start claude: not found ([Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../tabby_pool_wt/devloop/t369'))`. By then `t369` and `t369-cases` were gone and not in `git worktree list`. The ticket went stuck.
Inference (main session, not measured): the cases were the same afternoon as #15; a second issuer for the same ticket that ends (stuck) runs `Issuer.cleanup()` and removes the worktrees the first issuer still uses. Check this first; if it is not the cause, find what removed the worktree (grep every remove_worktree / prune / rmtree caller).
